questions.question: Explain when to use grams and when to use kilograms, giving one example of each from gogo's kitchen.
questions.expected_answer: Use grams for light things, such as a 10 g packet of yeast or a 500 g tub of margarine. Use kilograms for heavy things, such as a 5 kg bag of mielie meal. 1 kilogram is 1 000 grams.

questions.question: A kitchen scale is marked 0, 500 g and 1 kg, with 5 equal spaces between 0 and 500 g. The pointer is 3 marks after 500 g. What is the mass?
questions.expected_answer: Each space is 500 divided by 5, which is 100 g. 3 marks after 500 g is 500 plus 300, which is 800 g.

questions.question: Order 2 kg, 500 g, 5 kg and 1 500 g from lightest to heaviest and explain your method.
questions.expected_answer: Change all to grams: 2 000 g, 500 g, 5 000 g, 1 500 g. From lightest: 500 g, 1 500 g, 2 kg, 5 kg. Changing to the same unit makes the comparison fair.
